result.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
result.summary: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出随机动量传输：以概率 q 用廉价预测器代替 STORM 类方法每步额外的梯度校正，用重要性加权保持条件均值并量化方差代价，在若干假设下给出 LMO 更新的 O(T^{-1/3}) 平稳性界与在线预测器的收敛保证，并在 MNIST1D、CIFAR-10 上验证降低成本的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 「以廉价预测替代部分昂贵计算、再用重要性加权保持估计无偏」的机制，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK 的成本权衡（何时调用视觉证据、何时用 latent 预测推进状态）及贡献分配提供借鉴线索，但属另一领域的优化理论，迁移可行性需人工核查。
